title: Search-to-program boundary
summary: ResonantCortex2 asked whether successful search trajectories could be compressed into local modes and routed as a frozen reusable program. V0 found some local compressibility and cross-solver structure, but autonomous compiled execution failed, preserving an important boundary between finding useful trajectory fragments and acquiring an executable algorithm.

nodes.claim: Tests whether generic search can discover successful trajectories, compress them into local affine modes, route those modes by source-state geometry and execute the frozen mode bank as a reusable algorithm on held-out problems.
nodes.survived: Successful search traces can contain locally compressible structure, some cross-solver reuse geometry and post-hoc explanation fidelity.
nodes.killed: Algorithm compilation did not survive V0: local compression and shared trace geometry did not produce useful autonomous routed execution on the held-out tasks, making composition and routing the important boundary rather than search score alone.
